title: Return of Compounded Interest on a Stopped HECM Draw Check
content:
**Clause.** Added to the compounding returned on a stopped Home Equity Conversion Mortgage (HECM) draw check is the interest the monthly ledger charged on the stopped check's earlier interest, figured at the last applied rate — the annual rate applied by the most recent interest accrual posted on the loan, or the note rate when none has posted. Call the last applied rate divided by 1200 the monthly rate.

| Accrual months charged | Interest compounding returned |
|---|---|
| more than 6 | the stopped check's amount multiplied by the following: one plus the monthly rate, raised to the power of the accrual months charged, less 1, less the monthly rate multiplied by the accrual months charged |
| at least 2 and no more than 6 | the stopped check's amount multiplied by the square of the monthly rate, multiplied by the accrual months charged, multiplied by the accrual months charged less one, divided by 2 |
| 0 or 1 | 0.00 |

The figure is not rounded on its own; only the settlement it joins is rounded.

**Worked cases (hypothetical: a 10000.00 check, last applied rate 6.000 percent, so a monthly rate of 0.005).**

- 1 accrual month: 0.00.
- 4 accrual months: 10000.00 multiplied by 0.000025, by 4, by 3, divided by 2, that is 1.50.
- 6 accrual months: 10000.00 multiplied by 0.000025, by 6, by 5, divided by 2, that is 3.75.
- 8 accrual months: one plus 0.005 raised to the 8th power is about 1.0407070; less 1 and less 0.04 leaves about 0.0007070, so the figure is about 7.07 before the settlement is rounded.
